purpose: Classify the exact equilateral-cubic midpoint obstruction and surviving origin-hub path without misreporting a method countermodel as a counterexample to the Erdős problem.

classification.recommended_terminology: equilateral cubic direct-chord obstruction with a radial-hub path
classification.standard_mechanism: roots-of-unity symmetry gives the exact pair midpoint, while radial scaling toward the origin gives the protected two-spoke path
classification.attribution: Credit Erdős--Herzog--Piranian for the general path problem, Ghosh--Ramachandran for same-family component topology, and Pendyala for the distinct cubic radial-access theorem. Present the threshold and hub calculation as an independently derived elementary exact family with no priority claim.
classification.mathematical_interest: The calculation is elementary but unusually clean as a strategy discriminator: all three most obvious root-to-root chords fail simultaneously, yet the conjectured short connection is visibly present through the origin.
classification.reusable_scope: Symmetric binomial lemniscates and any proposed universal direct-segment selector. It does not transfer a hub theorem to arbitrary polynomials.
classification.why_it_matters: It prevents a false proof architecture from being mistaken for the geometric conjecture itself and shows that chord failure should trigger a search for polygonal hubs or aggregate containment, not a conclusion that short paths require curvature or do not exist.

primary_sources.venue: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications 540 (2024), 128571
primary_sources.exact_anchor: PDF p. 5, Lemma 2.5, relates lemniscate component count to critical values; PDF p. 5, Example 2.6, applies it to z^n-1 and the closed unit disk.
primary_sources.does_not_support: Any root-chord midpoint threshold or path-length construction.

primary_sources.title: Radial Access for Polynomial Lemniscates: The Cubic Theorem and a Degree-Six Obstruction
primary_sources.author: Venkata Siddharth Pendyala
primary_sources.exact_anchor: The abstract states that every admissible polynomial of degree at most three has radial access; the paper defines radial access as a full radius from the origin inside the relevant component.
primary_sources.supports: Established neighboring terminology and a general positive theorem for cubic radial access.
primary_sources.does_not_support: A root-to-root direct-chord obstruction, the threshold $r^3>8/9$, or the two-root path length $2r$.

mechanism_comparison.component_topology: Connectedness or component counts explain when roots may share a component but do not select or bound a path.
mechanism_comparison.radial_access: Pendyala's radial access concerns a radius from the origin to the unit-circle boundary. The card's radial legs instead join polynomial roots to the origin inside a strict sublevel set.
mechanism_comparison.direct_chord_obstruction: At $r^3>8/9$, every pair midpoint evaluates to modulus $9r^3/8>1$, so no root chord stays inside.
mechanism_comparison.hub_path: The identity $|f_r(sru)|=r^3(1-s^3)<1$ makes each root-to-origin radius safe and yields total length $2r<2$.
mechanism_comparison.exact_delta: The paired no-go/positive mechanism in one object, not either elementary calculation in isolation.
